q: The scientific study of the relationship between living organisms and their physical environment is called
exp: Ecology (term coined by Ernst Haeckel) studies organisms and their interactions with the environment.

q: In the food chain Grass → Grasshopper → Frog → Snake → Hawk, which organism is the secondary consumer?
exp: Grasshopper is the primary consumer; frog, which eats it, is the secondary consumer.

q: The Montreal Protocol (1987) was adopted to control the production and use of
exp: The Montreal Protocol phases out substances such as CFCs and halons that deplete the ozone layer.

q: The Chipko Movement, which involved hugging trees to prevent felling, began in the 1970s in which present-day state?
exp: Chipko began in Chamoli district (now Uttarakhand); Sunderlal Bahuguna and Gaura Devi are associated with it.

q: Which of the following is NOT a greenhouse gas?
exp: Greenhouse gases absorb infrared radiation; molecular nitrogen does not.

q: The Wildlife (Protection) Act of India was enacted in the year
exp: The Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 provides for protection of wild animals, birds and plants.

q: Ozone layer, which absorbs harmful ultraviolet rays, is present in which layer of the atmosphere?
exp: About 90% of atmospheric ozone lies in the stratosphere (15-35 km).

q: Which of the following pollutants is mainly responsible for acid rain?
options: Sulphur dioxide and oxides of nitrogen
exp: SO2 and NOx form sulphuric and nitric acids, lowering rain pH below 5.6.

q: According to Lindeman's 10 per cent law, how much energy is transferred from one trophic level to the next?
exp: Only about one-tenth of energy is passed to the next trophic level; the rest is lost as heat and respiration.

q: Which of the following is an ex-situ method of conserving biodiversity?
exp: Ex-situ conservation protects species outside their natural habitat, e.g. zoos, botanical gardens, seed banks.

q: Which of the following is NOT one of the biodiversity hotspots found in India?
exp: The Amazon basin is in South America; India has parts of Himalaya, Western Ghats, Indo-Burma and Sundaland hotspots.

q:
Statement I: Carbon dioxide is the main gas responsible for enhanced global warming due to human activities.
Statement II: Burning of fossil fuels and deforestation increase atmospheric CO2.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
exp: Fossil fuel burning and deforestation raise CO2, the largest contributor to anthropogenic warming.

q: Eutrophication of a lake is mainly caused by an excess of
exp: Nutrient enrichment causes algal blooms; decay of algae depletes dissolved oxygen.

q: The Indian Parliament enacted the Environment (Protection) Act in 1986 following which event?
exp: The Bhopal gas leak (1984) of methyl isocyanate prompted the umbrella Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.

q: The Kyoto Protocol, adopted in 1997, mainly aims at
options: Reducing greenhouse gas emissions of industrialised countries
Controlling trade in wild fauna and flora
Banning transboundary movement of hazardous wastes
exp: The Kyoto Protocol set legally binding GHG reduction targets for developed countries.

q: Biomagnification refers to the
options: Decrease in energy at higher trophic levels
Increase in concentration of a non-degradable toxin at successive trophic levels
exp: Substances such as DDT and mercury accumulate and are present in higher concentration at higher trophic levels.

q: The Silent Valley movement in Kerala was launched to oppose
options: A hydroelectric project on the Kunthipuzha river
A mining project in the Western Ghats
A highway through a tiger reserve
exp: The protest saved the Silent Valley rainforest and led to a National Park (1985).

q: The Ramsar Convention, 1971, deals with the conservation of
exp: Ramsar (Iran) Convention provides for wise use and conservation of wetlands.

q: Which of the following is a non-renewable source of energy?
exp: Natural gas is a fossil fuel formed over millions of years and cannot be replenished quickly.

q: A solar photovoltaic cell converts
exp: Photovoltaic cells (usually silicon) use the photoelectric effect to produce electricity from sunlight.

q: The major component of biogas is
exp: Biogas, produced by anaerobic decomposition of organic matter, contains about 55-65% methane.

q: Project Tiger was launched in India in the year
exp: Project Tiger started on 1 April 1973 from Jim Corbett National Park.

q: Which was the first biosphere reserve of India, established in 1986?
exp: The Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve was the first in India, covering parts of Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Karnataka.

q: Which statutory body at the national level is headed by the Prime Minister under the Disaster Management Act, 2005?
exp: NDMA, established under the 2005 Act, has the Prime Minister as chairperson.

q: Tsunamis are mostly caused by
exp: Sudden vertical displacement of the sea floor during undersea earthquakes generates tsunami waves.

q: The Brundtland Commission report 'Our Common Future' (1987) defined sustainable development as development that
options: Stops all use of natural resources
Meets present needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their needs
exp: This definition of sustainable development comes from the World Commission on Environment and Development.

q: How many Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) were adopted by the UN in 2015 for achievement by 2030?
exp: The 2030 Agenda adopted 17 SDGs with 169 targets; the Millennium Development Goals were eight.

q: Carbon monoxide is harmful to humans because it
options: Combines with haemoglobin to form carboxyhaemoglobin
exp: CO has far greater affinity for haemoglobin than oxygen, reducing oxygen transport.

q: The Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act was passed in India in
exp: The Water Act was passed in 1974; the Air Act followed in 1981.

q: Noise level is measured in
exp: The decibel (dB) is the unit of sound intensity level.

q: Minamata disease, first reported in Japan, is caused by poisoning from
exp: Methylmercury released in industrial waste accumulated in fish eaten by local people.

q: The Bhopal gas tragedy of December 1984 was caused by the leakage of
exp: Methyl isocyanate (MIC) leaked from the Union Carbide pesticide plant at Bhopal.

q: Which organisation maintains the Red Data Book (Red List) of threatened species?
exp: The International Union for Conservation of Nature maintains the IUCN Red List.

q: A species found only in a particular geographical area and nowhere else is called
exp: Endemic species are restricted to a specific region, e.g. lion-tailed macaque of the Western Ghats.

q: The first species to colonise bare rock in primary succession are usually
exp: Crustose lichens secrete acids that weather rock and start soil formation.

q: Free-living nitrogen-fixing bacteria in soil include
exp: Azotobacter fixes nitrogen without a host; Rhizobium lives symbiotically in legume root nodules.

q: The process by which plants release water vapour into the atmosphere is called
exp: Transpiration through stomata returns water to the atmosphere in the water cycle.

q: In an ecosystem, the pyramid of energy is always
exp: Energy decreases at each trophic level, so the energy pyramid cannot be inverted.

q: A lichen is an example of which type of ecological interaction?
exp: A lichen is an association of an alga (or cyanobacterium) and a fungus benefiting both.

q: Which gas listed below has the highest Global Warming Potential per molecule over 100 years?
exp: SF6 has a GWP of more than 20,000 times CO2.
